text:
You are one of 4 members of a group that stays together for 10 rounds.

Every round, all members act at the same time: each receives 20 tokens and splits them between their own account and the group account, using the split tool once.
- Each token in your own account pays you 1 point.
- Each token in the group account pays 0.75 points to every member of the group, you included, whoever put it there.

After each round you learn how many tokens the group account received in total and how many points you got. You never learn what any other member did.

calls.text: Round 1 of 10.

reply.thinking:
This is a classic public goods game: each token contributed returns 0.75 to all four members, making full cooperation socially optimal (everyone contributing 20 yields 60 each) while individual rationality points toward contributing nothing, since defecting while others cooperate nets more. This tension between the dominant strategy of free-riding and the group-optimal outcome of full contribution is what makes repeated play interesting.

Since this is round one with no history yet, I'll open cooperatively by contributing 20 to signal good faith and see how the other members respond before adjusting my strategy.
